mismatches.name: lock_crossfire
mismatches.observed: Encore/Disable/Taunt crossfire: native RNG seed at decision 5 (P2 turn-3 submission) is 6001,34311,34941,52953 but the reference is 15052,34342,22947,2979 — the native turn-3 resolution consumes a different number/order of draws. The other three interaction fixtures (imprison_shared_pool, charge_weather_recharge_switch, help_redirect_tie) pass.

mismatches.name: imprison_shared_pool
mismatches.observed: Native rejects the legal reference command at decision 5 (P2 "move 1, move 1 -1") with "invalid input: illegal joint action": the Imprison interaction over-restricts the served mask (a foe move that shares the imprisoned move set must be shown disabled, but the native joint validation rejects a command the reference accepts).
mismatches.root_cause: Root-cause analysis (verified against the pinned source, attempt reverted to keep the tree green): `Pokemon#getMoves(restrictData)` turns a `'hidden'` disable into `disabled = !restrictData`, so the SERVED request reports the move disabled while `Side#chooseMove` reads the unrestricted list (`hidden -> false`) and still ACCEPTS the choice; `onFoeBeforeMove` (priority 4) then refuses the move at execution. The native engine currently marks the move hard-disabled, so the served mask matches but the choice is rejected. A correct fix needs a separate display-only hidden flag carried through MoveState -> MoveChoice -> the candidate/validation filter `(!disabled || hidden)`, with the request still reporting `disabled || hidden`; the first attempt (commit c0818d1's uncommitted sibling) got the acceptance right but broke the disable-family corpus, so it needs the candidate/validation filter and the state.rs restore reconstruction updated together.

analysis_note:
Root-cause analysis (verified against the pinned source, attempt reverted to keep the tree green): `Pokemon#getMoves(restrictData)` turns a `'hidden'` disable into `disabled = !restrictData`, so the SERVED request reports the move disabled while `Side#chooseMove` reads the unrestricted list (`hidden -> false`) and still ACCEPTS the choice; `onFoeBeforeMove` (priority 4) then refuses the move at execution. The native engine currently marks the move hard-disabled, so the served mask matches but the choice is rejected. A correct fix needs a separate display-only hidden flag carried through MoveState -> MoveChoice -> the candidate/validation filter `(!disabled || hidden)`, with the request still reporting `disabled || hidden`; the first attempt (commit c0818d1's uncommitted sibling) got the acceptance right but broke the disable-family corpus, so it needs the candidate/validation filter and the state.rs restore reconstruction updated together.

Additional evidence from the second fix attempt (reverted): applying the display-only hidden flag end-to-end made the Imprison choice acceptable, but then the pre-existing corpus fixture `disable_family_imprison_shared_moves_6` failed at decision 13 (P1 'move 1, move 1 1', turn 5) — the native candidate/validation path rejected a choice the reference accepts. At that boundary the served request (step 12 expected state) shows P1's slot-1 with ALL THREE moves `disabled: true` (world volatiles: `disable`; the foe holds `imprison`), yet the reference accepted a move choice. So the request's disabled flags are not the whole legality story: the fix must model the reference's actual choice-legality source (`getMoves()` unrestricted view: `disabled === 'hidden'` -> false, hard boolean -> true; PP>0 required) separately from the *served* request flags, and must explain why the reference accepts a choice whose served request shows every move disabled. Next attempt should start by dumping the reference's `pokemon.getMoves()` in both modes at that boundary against the native state.
